Thermite's plans are public. This page sums them up; the plan files in the repository hold every detail.

## v0.1.0, the first public release

**v0.1.0** is Thermite's first public release. With it, a tester can:

- install Thermite from published images;
- run agents on a sample project, with a free model or their own key;
- add rigs on their own machines over SSH and on their Kubernetes clusters;
- launch GPU rigs on RunPod.

Thermite's core is built: the judge, control and its dashboard, the agents, and the advisors that supervise them. This site describes what is built today, including these goals of this release:

- a research folder for each research run, which its workers search with ordinary tools and add to, and which a finished campaign exports with its report. It is done ([goal 062](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/062-research-folder.goal); [Research](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research));
- the dashboard's new campaign, run and live views, with steering as one message box. It is done ([goal 063](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/063-scan-and-steer.goal));
- dashboard buttons that say at once that a click took, and show its outcome without a refresh, such as a rig check that goes from sent to running to its result. It is done ([goal 080](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/080-buttons-show-progress.goal); [On the dashboard](../reference/signed-commands.md#on-the-dashboard));
- one experiment queue for each run, which the planner coordinates. It is done ([goal 064](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/064-experiment-queue.goal));
- journals and a research corpus from every campaign: the agents' field notes, research in every mode, and Thermite's own knowledge base, with a collection for each campaign that holds everything its runs produce and that later runs' workers, planner and advisors search. It is done ([goal 065](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/065-journals-and-corpus.goal));
- rules for the planner that name the run's directions, in plain words or picked as `:name:` on the run's **Planner** tab. It is done ([goal 066](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/066-direction-rules.goal); [Make a rule: tell the planner](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md#make-a-rule-tell-the-planner));
- MCP servers for a campaign's agents, named by its kit. It is done ([goal 068](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/068-mcp-servers-for-agents.goal); [Give agents MCP tools](../how-to/campaigns/give-agents-mcp-tools.md));
- copying a campaign under a new name, with its own empty collection in the knowledge base, to give a second model the same campaign from zero: **Copy** on the campaign's page, and its twins over REST, MCP and the command line. It is done ([goal 069](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/069-copy-a-campaign.goal); [Compare two models from zero](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md#compare-two-models-from-zero));
- a claim's source named by the address its page was archived from or its file name in the research folder, as well as by its id, still checked word for word, and each draft's reasons in the run's **History**. It is done ([goal 076](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/076-claim-sources-and-reasons.goal); [Research](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research));
- archiving a campaign, which keeps its folder, and folders for campaigns in the dashboard's left navigation, which no longer lists the rigs. It is done ([goal 077](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/077-archive-and-folders.goal); [Archive campaigns and sort them into folders](../how-to/campaigns/archive-and-folders.md));
- the judge's findings in view: a held-out failure named by its case and kind for the owner and by its kind alone for the agents, a refused change's violations wherever the change is looked at, a time limit for each kit cell, and each goal's real check on the campaign's and the run's pages. It is done ([goal 082](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/082-judge-findings-in-view.goal); [Held-out failures](../reference/verdicts.md#held-out-failures));
- a cap on the context window of each agent's model, and compaction near it: an agent's conversation is kept, summarized and goes on, in every harness, the advisors' included. A campaign can set its own window and compaction point for its runs. The rig's are set on **Edit rig** and over REST and MCP; a campaign's on **New campaign**, **Copy** and its page, and over REST, MCP and the command line. It is done ([goal 070](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/070-model-context-cap.goal); [Set an agent's context window and compaction](../how-to/models/model-per-agent.md#set-an-agents-context-window-and-compaction));
- a harness of the owner's choice for every kind of agent, not only the workers: Pi, OpenCode v2, Claude Code or the Codex CLI for the planner and each advisor too, in **Runs in** on **Edit rig**. It is done ([goal 073](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/073-harness-for-each-agent.goal); [Where each agent runs](../how-to/models/model-per-agent.md#where-each-agent-runs));
- one name for each agent, the same on every screen, page, field and tool, in two groups: the work (the workers and the planner) and the advisors (the teachers, one or two, with a merged by model for two, the auditor and the review panel). It is done ([goal 074](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/074-one-name-for-each-agent.goal); [Give each agent its own model](../how-to/models/model-per-agent.md));
- model use and cost: every model call the agents make is counted by code, and summed for a run, a campaign and the whole system, on a run's page, a campaign's page and **Metrics**, and over REST and MCP. The cost uses **Model prices** in **Settings › Providers**. It is done ([goal 075](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/075-model-usage.goal); [Model use and cost](../reference/model-use.md));
- less overhead and fewer stops: a provider's error is sorted by its kind, so a rate limit waits and a refused key or no credits stops the run's agents and asks you; no hidden default caps; a rig can finish its running trials before an image update; a restart keeps a trial's counters and the lanes' caches; and a win is promoted once the auditor clears it, unless you ask to decide first. It is done ([goal 079](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/079-thermite-overhead.goal); [Promotions](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md#promotions));
- a campaign's brief for every mode, on its own step of **New campaign**: additional information in Markdown, starting links, ideas to try and hypotheses, which the planner, the workers and the advisors get. It is done ([goal 078](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/078-campaign-brief.goal); [The brief](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md#2-the-brief));
- a queue that stays full of ideas: the teachers' main product is a portfolio of new opportunities, written to the queue, and they read the champion's code, the attempts' diffs and the judge's reasons; a campaign keeps a target of experiments ready, **Ideas kept ready**, and a queue below it asks the planner and then the teachers for more; lanes propose their follow-ups. It is done ([goal 081](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/081-ideas-first.goal); [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#the-teachers));
- a goal report that keeps what it measured: a goal checked by the kit's verifier gives each measured case's values, met or not, as a threshold goal does, on the run's **Goals** block and to the agents, never a held-out case's; and no new trial while the judge checks a second time a champion that met every required goal, a check that also runs the held-out cases of the goals met. It is done ([goal 086](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/086-goal-report-values-and-confirmation-wait.goal); [The goal report](../reference/verdicts.md#the-goal-report));
- closing a run by hand: **Close run** on a run's page, and `close_run` with the owner's token, end a run you no longer want for good, with your reason, as a run that met its goals ends. It is done ([goal 087](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/087-close-a-run.goal); [Close a run](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#close-a-run));
- a kit written elsewhere, given to control as a git bundle of its repository: control keeps it with its commits, and rigs fetch it from control by commit. It is done ([goal 096](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/096-kits-from-elsewhere.goal); [Give control a kit you wrote elsewhere](../how-to/campaigns/write-a-kit.md#give-control-a-kit-you-wrote-elsewhere));
- teachers that read what their run has found before they propose its next steps, read only: its sources with the text the harness archived, its claims, hypotheses and findings, its notes, its report and the files its lanes wrote. It is done ([goal 098](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/098-research-teachers-read-the-research.goal); [What they read](../explanation/supervision.md#what-they-read));
- status words that say how a run ended: **Completed** for a goal run whose goals were met and confirmed, or a research run whose questions are answered, and **Finished** for any other closed run. A campaign shows its newest run's word, and a run started with its agents off says `judge only` on its page. It is done ([goal 099](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/099-campaign-status-words.goal); [Run labels on the dashboard](../reference/verdicts.md#run-labels-on-the-dashboard));
- the local stack's rig on everything its machine has: every CPU and all the memory that Docker or Podman has, and, on Linux, every NVIDIA GPU, through `compose.gpu.yaml`, which `thermite local init` writes when it finds them. `thermite doctor` and `local init` say what the rig gets on each kind of machine, AMD GPUs and a Mac's Apple GPU included, which it can't use yet. It is done: checked on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU under Podman ([goal 037](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/037-gpu-compose.goal); [What the rig gets](../how-to/install/one-machine.md#what-the-rig-gets));
- exports from the dashboard: **Export** on a rig's or a run's page, of what changed or a full one that holds every run's research folder, finished or not, and an **Exports** page that downloads each export as one archive. It is built; its last check, a research run's full export that holds the run's final paper, waits for the research run's end below ([goal 103](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/103-export-and-download.goal); [Get a rig's results from control](../how-to/operate/exports-on-control.md));
- a research run that ends when its questions are answered: after its minimum duration, the review panel decides each question and each required hypothesis, code checks each answer's citations and numbers, and the run ends once every item has an end, hands-off unless the run asks you about reviews, with a research paper that the final writer writes and code checks; its next experiments go to the knowledge base for other runs. A campaign may set a floor of verified claims before the first review. It is built; its check on a deployment is goal 117's acceptance runs, below ([goal 112](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/112-research-ends-when-answered.goal); [When a research run ends](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#when-a-research-run-ends));
- research that answers its questions: one living answer card for each question, written from the run's verified claims with its certainty and the gaps in its evidence, and checked by code; work driven by those gaps, which stops for a question that is answered or saturated; hypotheses in a pool, merged when they repeat, of which only the author's and the promoted ones need a verdict; review decisions that stand until a card changes; and the progress rule, which ends a run whose open questions have stopped adding. It is built; its acceptance runs on a deployment are the last step before the release ([goal 117](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/117-research-that-answers.goal); [Research](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research));
- a hill climb that starts from a measured point: the judge's first job is the run's baseline, which measures the starting point alone on every case, and no trial starts before it. Each guard's total allowance holds against the baseline. A starting point that can't be measured yet puts the run in setup, where the workers make it build and run and the judge checks their changes. It is done ([goal 115](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/115-hill-climb-baseline.goal); [Hill climb](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#hill-climb));
- a **Reviews** tab and a **Hypotheses** tab for a research run: every review, each reviewer's answers and comments, and the outcome; each hypothesis with its status and verdict, which the owner promotes, returns to the pool or retires. It is done ([goal 116](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/116-reviews-tab.goal));
- `get_run` answers of a size an agent can read for a run that worked for a day or more: each long list cut to its newest entries, with a count of the rest and a way to page through it, and the same for one run over REST. It is done ([goal 128](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/128-get-run-bounded.goal));
- a hill climb's real metric values beside each gain, such as `412 → 614 tok/s` beside `+49.0%`: on each attempt, the champions, the gain chart, the campaign's headline and the leaderboard. It is done ([goal 133](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/133-metric-values-beside-gains.goal));
- a subscription's usage windows on **Providers**: a Claude subscription's, as Claude Code reports them, and, for a ChatGPT subscription, OpenAI's answer when control asks. It is done ([goal 151](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/151-plan-usage-on-providers.goal));
- lanes that keep working while the judge works, if a campaign asks for it, a judge that builds two changes at once, and changes carried to a new champion. It is done ([goal 135](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/135-lanes-and-judge-throughput.goal)).

Also built:

- a release workflow and bundle, and `thermite doctor`;
- version checks between control and rigs, with each rig's version and reporting state on the dashboard;
- a sample project;
- the Codex CLI as a worker harness for a ChatGPT subscription ([Run the agents in Codex](../how-to/models/chatgpt-subscription.md#run-the-agents-in-codex));
- Start a run over REST, MCP and the command line, as well as from the campaign's page;
- rigs on RunPod ([Run a rig on RunPod](../how-to/install/runpod-rig.md)). The owner launches them from the dashboard or over REST, MCP and the command line, and stops, starts and terminates them. A RunPod rig can stop by itself when no run is at work on it. It works on the pod's own disk and keeps a snapshot of its state on the pod's volume, so a stop and a start keep its work. Its page shows the pod's log, before the rig enrolls too ([A pod that runs but never enrolls](../how-to/install/runpod-rig.md#a-pod-that-runs-but-never-enrolls-read-its-log)). A launch, its enrollment and checks, a stop and a terminate were run on a real GPU pod ([goal 025](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/025-runpod-tests-and-docs.goal));
- web search for research runs, through an MCP server the campaign names, done ahead of v0.5.0 ([goal 046](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/046-web-search.goal); [Give agents MCP tools](../how-to/campaigns/give-agents-mcp-tools.md));
- sign-in with a real Claude or ChatGPT subscription, each tested from start to end: sign in, give a rig the model, pass its model check, and run a trial whose change the judge confirmed ([goal 009](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/_completed/009-subscription-sign-in-tests.goal); [Use a Claude subscription](../how-to/models/claude-subscription.md), [Use a ChatGPT subscription](../how-to/models/chatgpt-subscription.md)).

The release publishes the images and their bundle, each image checked before it got its version's tag, with the CUDA 13 harness image labelled untested because it has not run on a GPU yet ([Known limits](../reference/known-limits.md#the-cuda-13-harness-is-untested)).

These ship as built, and each one's last check runs on a deployment after the release: exports from the dashboard, above ([goal 103](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/103-export-and-download.goal)); no idle lanes, with a drain that says which trials it waits for ([goal 136](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/136-no-idle-lanes.goal)); a trial's session read over MCP ([goal 139](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/139-trial-session-over-mcp.goal)); a long tool call that doesn't stall the process that streams it ([goal 140](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/140-long-tool-call-no-stall.goal)); a hill climb's champion value at the top of its run's page ([goal 142](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/142-champion-value-on-run-page.goal)); a trial's clock, with the time left and a lane's build cache that works across its trials ([goal 144](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/144-trial-clock.goal)); and an optional limit on the field notes a worker writes in one reply ([goal 147](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/goals/147-notes-per-turn.goal)).

The [roadmap file](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/roadmap.md) lists every v0.1.0 goal with its status, and the [release plan](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/release-v0.1.0.md) gives the release's scope and the steps to ship it.

## Later versions

Later versions are proposed: their order and contents can change. Each one ships when its goals are verified, not on a date.

| Version | Focus |
| --- | --- |
| **v0.1.1** | Code clean-up, in two steps: a read-only look at the whole code that writes a guide to the changes, then the clean-up itself, area by area. Then the code follows Thermite's conventions, with files of a size you can review, in folders, no duplicated knowledge or dead code, and the engineering rules for design, errors, limits, logging, security and tests, so that later changes are easier. |
| **v0.1.2** | GPUs on demand, and work within a budget: GPUs rented only while they work, for the judge and for the workers' checks; a secondary judge that asks an outside service, such as a contest's own judge, on a schedule and only when the champion gained; one budget in dollars for a run, easy to set, that holds on every rig; a setting that turns off the judge's repeated measurements, for measurements that are slow or cost money; hill-climb contracts that run a check once for each change, run held-out cases for less, and say what does not count, as goal contracts do; in **Settings › Providers**, all that Thermite spent on a GPU cloud, not only its test pods; a run's use of its rig's CPUs, memory and GPUs; and rig images for each GPU generation, each rig set up from the one that fits its GPUs. |
| **v0.1.3** | Follow-ups to the first release: a kit bundle given to control from the dashboard, gated models on cloud rigs, a research campaign's copy that takes its own rubrics, MCP clients that see control's new tools after an update, a drain that doesn't wait for a trial that started seconds before it, a rig's supervisor restarted or updated alone, a waiting win the champion moved past, a command's result that says its output was cut only when it was, and a model check that waits as long as the rig says on a busy model. |
| **v0.1.4** | UI clean-up and UX improvements: every screen checked against the rules for screens; small faults found in use fixed, such as a campaign's **Agents' context** that lists rigs its runs never used; **New campaign**'s buttons show they were pressed; an **Info** tab with everything a campaign and a run were started with; a stuck rig in **Needs you**; the model's reasoning and words on **Live**, not only its tool calls; a **Copy** button by each ID; an **Exports** page that shows each rig's full exports first, with the smaller ones folded; a judge-only run whose goals fill in as the judge checks them; a run that says why nothing is at work; **New campaign** and a run's page that set whether its lanes keep working while the judge works; and faster dashboard pages. |
| **v0.2.0** | Run Thermite without the dashboard: every dashboard action has an API and MCP twin, all logs are in one place you can search, and you sign in with your identity provider. Also planned: a deep-research teacher that runs when the queue needs ideas, research tasks with web search inside goal and hill-climb runs, a run that starts from a champion on another rig, a hill climb that improves several metrics one after the other, a **Knowledge** page to explore the knowledge base, with copies of it in outside stores, kits that define how a campaign runs, with their own images, on rigs that are only the slots it runs in, several runs at once on one rig when they fit, and AMD GPUs and Apple silicon in rigs. |
| **v0.3.0** | Rigs you can trust: checks before a rig is deployed, setup and removal that are safe to repeat, upgrades from control, lanes kept off the local network, and a cloud rig that can move to another GPU, keeping its state. |
| **v0.4.0** | Kits and evidence: kits are easier to write and to test before agents start, and each result shows clearer evidence. Also planned: a research lab, one campaign that researches, builds, improves and researches again. |
| **v0.5.0** | Unattended for days: campaigns in all three modes run for days with no one watching. Also planned: a start in two commands. |
| **Later** | Ideas with no version yet, such as more kinds of target, planning across rigs, and a new run that reuses the judge's goal report when it starts from the same point. |

After v0.1.0, version numbers count up by the middle number: 0.2.0, 0.3.0 and so on. Fixes and quick follow-ups ship as 0.1.1, 0.1.2. A 0.x version makes no promise about upgrades.

## The plan files

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [Roadmap](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/roadmap.md) | Every goal, by version, in priority order, one line each |
| [Release plan for v0.1.0](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/release-v0.1.0.md) | The first release: its scope, its goals and the steps that shipped it |
| [Settled decisions](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/decisions.md) | Decisions that shape the whole product, with their dates |
| [How Thermite is planned](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/blob/main/docs/plan/README.md) | What a goal is, what each status means, and how an idea becomes a goal |

Each roadmap item is a **goal**: one file that says what it delivers, why, when it is done, and how it is going. Pages on this site link to a goal when they mention something that is not built yet.

To suggest an idea or ask about the plans, see [Getting help](getting-help.md).
